answer: Main analysis complete per your constraints. HEADLINE (positive-wealth only; composite==0 = missing-by-convention, negatives excluded): 1990->1996 Gini fell 0.688->0.623 for white males (-0.066, bootstrap 95% CI -0.094..-0.036) and 0.681->0.599 for white females (-0.082, CI -0.110..-0.052); p90/p50 fell 5.68->3.89 (male, CI on change -2.51..-1.09) and 4.89->3.74 (female, -1.76..-0.71); top-10% share fell 53.8%->47.8% and 52.1%->45.6%; top-1% share halved (18.5%->11.4%; 19.0%->11.7%); median among wealth-holders roughly tripled ($48.1k->$131.5k male, $58.4k->$132.0k female) and mean/median fell (2.61->1.83; 2.30->1.76). CO-PRIMARY SENSITIVITY (zeros kept, negatives floored): Gini rises slightly - male 0.780->0.793 (+0.013, CI -0.005..+0.035), female 0.761->0.777 (+0.016, CI -0.004..+0.038) - both increases small with CIs including zero; p90/p50 explodes (13.8->37.5; 12.1->37.6) purely mechanically as the pooled median collapses toward zero with zero-reporters rising 25.7%->43.3% (male) and 20.3%->42.6% (female); top-10% share flat (0.617->0.618; 0.587->0.591). Sign flip displayed, not hidden. ROBUST UNDER BOTH CONVENTIONS: p90/p75 (avoids the zero-contaminated median) falls under both (male 2.02->1.89 pos, 2.35->2.25 zk; female 1.88->1.85, 2.23->2.17) and top shares never rise. Third convention (zeros=missing, debtors kept at 0) reproduces the headline (dGini -0.068 male, -0.088 female). PANEL SENSITIVITY AGREES with cross-section: paired 1990&1996-positive subsample male n=1,732 Gini 0.676->0.613 (d=-0.063, CI -0.089..-0.037), female n=1,827 0.666->0.589 (d=-0.077, CI -0.102..-0.048); zero-flows 675/841 positive-in-1990 reading zero in 1996 vs 108/97 the other way, plus mean within-person log wealth change +0.80/+0.82 and 75%/73% increasing -> asymmetry supports coded non-response rather than wealth loss. GROUP CONTRAST (female change - male change): dGini(pos) -0.016 (CI -0.056..+0.025, p~0.47), dp90/p50(pos) +0.64 (CI -0.40..+1.46, p~0.26), dtop10 -0.006 (p~0.85); n's comparable (3,469 vs 3,630) and the bootstrap CIs, not the n's, show the male/female difference is indistinguishable from noise => parallel convergence, not divergence; by 1996 median wealth-holder is ~$132k in both cells and female Gini is slightly below male in both years. ever_jailed reported descriptively only: white/female 12/3,630 (0.33%), white/male 57/3,469 (1.64%). 1985 kept as background only (Gini 0.741/0.717; top10 61.6%/55.2%; p90/p50 8.07/9.72). FINAL HYPOTHESIS: Between 1990 and 1996 wealth inequality narrowed substantially for both white men and white women in this NLSY79 cohort, through top-end compression and rapid middle gains, and the two groups moved together rather than diverging. Among wealth-holders the Gini fell 0.688->0.623 (male) and 0.681->0.599 (female), p90/p50 fell 5.68->3.89 and 4.89->3.74, top-10% shares fell 53.8%->47.8% and 52.1%->45.6% and top-1% shares roughly halved, while median holdings roughly tripled (~$48k->~$132k; ~$58k->~$132k) - so the middle grew fastest and the top pulled away less. The narrowing also holds within respondents observed with positive wealth in both years and when debtors are kept at zero, so it is not selection into the positive-wealth sample. Only the aggregate Gini that treats every zero/blank as real zero wealth moves the other way (+0.013/+0.016, CIs including zero), mechanically from a doubling of zero values in 1996 that is better read as coded non-response; upper-tail ratios that avoid that zero-contaminated median (p90/p75) fall under both conventions. Thus inequality among wealth-holders narrowed decisively while measured dispersion including non-holders did not rise significantly - no evidence of rising wealth concentration - and the male-female difference in these changes (-0.016 Gini, CI -0.056..+0.025) is indistinguishable from noise, indicating parallel convergence.

payload.hypothesis: Between 1990 and 1996 wealth inequality narrowed substantially for both white men and white women in this NLSY79 cohort, driven by compression at the top and rapid gains in the middle of the wealth-holding distribution, and the two groups moved in parallel rather than diverging. Among respondents reporting positive wealth (headline basis: composite>0, zeros treated as missing-by-convention non-response, negatives/debt excluded) the Gini fell from 0.688 to 0.623 (-0.066, 95% CI -0.094..-0.036) for white males and 0.681 to 0.599 (-0.082, CI -0.110..-0.052) for white females; p90/p50 fell 5.68->3.89 and 4.89->3.74; the top-10% wealth share fell 53.8%->47.8% and 52.1%->45.6% and the top-1% share roughly halved (18.5%->11.4%; 19.0%->11.7%), while median holdings among wealth-holders roughly tripled (~$48k->~$132k male; ~$58k->~$132k female) and mean/median ratios fell (2.61->1.83; 2.30->1.76). Inequality therefore compressed top-down: the middle and lower-middle of the wealth-holding distribution grew fastest and the top pulled away less. The same narrowing holds within respondents observed with positive wealth in both years (dGini -0.063 male, -0.077 female, both CIs excluding zero) and when debtors are retained at zero (dGini -0.068/-0.089), so it is not an artifact of selection into the positive-wealth sample. The only statistic moving the other way is the aggregate Gini that counts every zero/blank composite as genuinely zero wealth: 0.780->0.793 (male) and 0.761->0.777 (female), increases of just +0.013/+0.016 whose bootstrap CIs include zero, generated mechanically by the share of respondents at exactly zero doubling (25.7%->43.3% male, 20.3%->42.6% female) in 1996 - a pattern far better explained by coded non-response than by a collapse in holdings (675/841 respondents who held positive wealth in 1990 read as zero in 1996, versus 108/97 in reverse, while mean within-person log wealth rose ~0.80). The apparent p90/p50 explosion under that convention (13.8->37.5; 12.1->37.6) is a median artifact, and upper-tail ratios that avoid it (p90/p75) fall under both conventions while top shares stay flat. In short, inequality among wealth-holders narrowed decisively while measured dispersion including non-holders did not rise significantly, so there is no evidence of increasing wealth concentration for young white adults in this period; 1985 background values (Gini 0.741/0.717, top-10% share 61.6%/55.2%) show the decline already underway and continuing. The male-female contrast is not distinguishable from noise: female-minus-male difference-in-differences is -0.016 Gini points (CI -0.056..+0.025, p~0.47) and +0.64 for p90/p50 (CI -0.40..+1.46, p~0.26), and by 1996 the median wealth-holder stands at about $132k in both cells - parallel convergence rather than divergence, with white women entering 1990 with slightly higher median holdings and slightly lower inequality than white men.
payload.workflow: 1) Inspection: 12,013 rows x 6 cols; zero true missing values; race white/black/hipanic 7099/3013/1901; sex female/male 6164/5849; ever_jailed 1 = 289. 2) Built group x year statistic panel for white_male and white_female for 1985 (background), 1990, 1996 under three conventions: pos (headline: composite>0), zk (co-primary: zeros kept, negatives floored at 0), pneg0 (zeros dropped as missing, debtors kept at 0) plus a raw-scale context block. 3) Statistics per cell/year/convention: basis n, share zero, share negative, mean, SD, SD of log wealth among positives, median, p10, p25, p75, p90, p95, p90/p50, p90/p75, p75/p25, p90/p10, mean/median, top-10% and top-1% shares, Gini. 4) 1990->1996 change table for Gini, p90/p50, p90/p75, top-10% share with 1,000-replicate bootstrap 95% CIs (independent resampling of the two years = conservative). 5) Difference-in-differences female change minus male change with bootstrap CIs and two-sided tail p-values, all three conventions. 6) Paired within-respondent sensitivity restricted to positive wealth in both 1990 and 1996 (male n=1,732, female n=1,827) with paired bootstrap on dGini, plus zero-flow tabulation. 7) ever_jailed reported descriptively only. Outputs: out/group_year_table.csv, change_table_bootstrap.csv, diff_in_diff.csv, paired_sensitivity.csv, ever_jailed_descriptives.csv, zero_missing_by_convention.csv, results_summary.md, run_log.txt.
